endorsements.quote: The human panels used to train the algorithms should include patient representatives.

The algorithms also could be more just, validated to be neutral to socioeconomic status, race, gender, age, and other social factors except insofar as these factors represent risk factors for, or change the effectiveness of treatment.
In addition, the use of race, gender, age, and social determinants of health in DL algorithms for PA would need to be carefully reviewed, as inclusion can have unintended consequences.
Even so, the potential for occult biases should be continually re-examined through periodic reviews of performance as part of governance.

unlisted_practices: Use explainable AI methodologies in prior authorization algorithms to ensure transparency.
Subject prior authorization AI algorithms to objective public review and certification against a panel of clinical cases juried by national clinical leaders.
Combine AI-based prior authorization with a human-based oversight and appeal process.
Train prior authorization AI on consensus human judgments from expert panels representing patients, payers, and providers.
Stage implementation of AI for prior authorization because of potential bias, starting with existing foundation models to demonstrate feasibility.
Curate a nationally representative healthcare data set if AI-based prior authorization efforts prove successful.
Standardize the clinical data providers submit for prior authorization requests and limit it to the minimum necessary.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary proposing a human-centric AI-driven approach for prior authorization review.
